purpose: Narrowly harden crash, torn-reservation, result-visibility, and abandoned-attempt recovery semantics without changing the frozen oracle, execution profile, event schema, result schema, quality gates, prompt, provider, R03, or R04.

definitions.attempt_start_boundary: The original boundary remains: attempt_reserved must be created exclusively, fully written, flushed, and durably synchronized before provider construction or any provider request.
definitions.provisional_reservation_artifact: The attempt lifecycle path after exclusive creation but before the creating process has successfully crossed the attempt_start_boundary.
definitions.post_crash_valid_reservation_record: A later process can parse and fully validate a lifecycle journal whose first event is the frozen attempt_reserved event, even though that later process cannot prove the historical fsync boundary.
definitions.ambiguous_torn_reservation_artifact: An existing attempt lifecycle path that is empty, malformed, truncated, or otherwise cannot be validated as a journal beginning with attempt_reserved.
definitions.result_visibility_boundary: For failure and recovery decisions, result bytes are potentially inspectable once an attempt-scoped result temporary artifact or the canonical result artifact exists.
definitions.deterministic_result_finalization: Zero-provider recovery that validates surviving complete result bytes, establishes or verifies the canonical result artifact, appends result_published when missing, computes frozen technical validity only, and appends the matching bound attempt_terminated event.
definitions.series_blocked: No later real-provider attempt may start in this baseline series until a separately governed manual forensic resolution policy exists and is explicitly authorized. This addendum defines no destructive or manual repair policy.

trusted_local_host_boundary.assumption: The repository working directory is not concurrently manipulated by a malicious local process during reservation, publication, or recovery.
trusted_local_host_boundary.filesystem_identity_guarantee: Conditional path/inode checks are best-effort race detection, not a portable atomic compare-and-unlink guarantee.

cleanup_requirements: the creating process still owns the descriptor created by exclusive creation
the process has not successfully crossed attempt_start_boundary
the current path is still observed to identify the owned inode immediately before cleanup
no detected replacement path is deleted
directory removal durability is synchronized where supported

later_process_valid_reservation_record.rationale: A later process cannot safely distinguish a durably synchronized reservation from a full reservation record that survived abrupt loss before the original fsync returned. Conservative consumption prevents unsafe attempt-number reuse.

before_result_visibility_boundary.condition: No attempt-scoped temporary result artifact and no canonical result artifact survives the failure.

at_or_after_result_visibility_boundary.preferred_live_action: If deterministic finalization can be completed safely in the live process, complete it. Otherwise leave the attempt nonterminal and require explicit zero-provider recovery.
at_or_after_result_visibility_boundary.reason: Potentially inspectable result bytes make a later fresh provider attempt vulnerable to result shopping.

requirements: temporary bytes validate as the complete frozen result
recovery publishes exactly those validated bytes without provider calls
published canonical bytes are synchronized and re-read
recovery_events: append result_published with canonical path and SHA-256
append the bound technical terminal derived only from frozen technical validity

requirements: canonical bytes validate as the complete frozen result
canonical bytes are synchronized and re-read
SHA-256 is computed from the re-read canonical bytes
recovery_events: append result_published with canonical path and SHA-256
append the bound technical terminal derived only from frozen technical validity

requirements: event path equals the canonical attempt path
canonical bytes validate as the complete frozen result
result lifecycle case IDs and operational statuses agree with the journal
recovery_events: append only the bound technical terminal derived only from frozen technical validity

requirements: temporary and canonical bytes both validate
temporary and canonical bytes are byte-identical
canonical bytes are synchronized and re-read
temporary cleanup, if attempted, must not delete a detected replacement
recovery_events: append the bound technical terminal derived only from frozen technical validity

examples: temporary result exists but does not validate
canonical result exists but does not validate
result_published digest does not match canonical bytes
result lifecycle binding does not match the journal
result artifact cannot be read or synchronized safely

result_recovery_may_append: result_published if and only if a valid canonical result exists or is deterministically established and the event is missing

implementation_requirements: Bind this addendum by exact SHA-256 before any real attempt reservation.
Validate the base lifecycle contract and all governing frozen hashes before applying addendum logic.
Keep the existing event schema and result schema unchanged.
Do not create a second persistent lock file.
Hold the original lifecycle journal lock throughout live execution and explicit recovery.
Never call the provider from recovery.
Never automatically rerun a real attempt.
Never overwrite an existing lifecycle or canonical result artifact.
Do not append an unbound terminal after the result_visibility_boundary.
Do not silently delete an ambiguous torn reservation artifact.
Do not permit a later attempt after any series_blocked classification.
Use only the frozen technical validity gate to select a bound recovered terminal.
Treat quality metrics as irrelevant to whether recovery chooses technically_valid or technically_invalid.
Revalidate Git HEAD and allowed worktree artifacts before and after recovery appends.
acceptance_test_matrix: ordinary zero-byte pre-start write failure cleans owned provisional path and consumes no attempt
ordinary partial first-write failure cleans only the proven owned provisional path and consumes no attempt
ordinary first fsync failure cleans only the proven owned provisional path and consumes no attempt
detected path replacement is never deleted
post-crash valid attempt_reserved-only journal is conservatively treated as consumed
post-crash empty or malformed reservation artifact blocks the series and makes zero provider calls
publication failure before any surviving result artifact may terminate as technically_invalid/result_publication_failed
failure after a valid temporary result exists cannot append an unbound technical terminal
failure after canonical result creation cannot append interrupted, unexpected_execution_failure, or unbound result_publication_failed
valid temp-only abandoned state is deterministically finalized with zero provider calls
valid canonical result without result_published event is synchronized, attested, and deterministically finalized
valid canonical result with result_published event receives only the matching bound technical terminal
valid temp and canonical artifacts must be byte-identical before deterministic finalization
invalid or inconsistent surviving result artifact blocks the series and appends no terminal
recovered technically valid quality-pass result blocks later attempts
recovered technically valid quality-fail result also blocks later attempts
recovered technically invalid complete result allows only the explicit next attempt after preservation commit
KeyboardInterrupt after result visibility cannot produce an unbound interrupted terminal
SystemExit after result visibility cannot produce an unbound interrupted terminal
ordinary exception after result visibility cannot produce unbound unexpected_execution_failure
recovery performs zero provider calls, zero network calls, and reads no OpenAI API key
recovery never rewrites prior lifecycle bytes
recovery never overwrites the canonical result target
all recovery events retain the original sut_commit and frozen contract bindings
privacy sentinels remain absent from lifecycle, operator output, and unauthorized temporary content
